title: Send a personal email now
summary: Immediately send the caller's plain-text message and optional attachments to the fixed personal recipient, with optional reply routing and thread headers.
use_when: The user explicitly asks to send an email now to their fixed personal inbox and supplies or approves the subject, body, and any attachment filenames and bytes.
A previously drafted message should now be sent exactly as approved.
An installed local product has explicit standing authority for its defined immediate notification, owns the occurrence and exact frozen message, and supplies a stable idempotency key.
do_not_use_when: The user asks only to draft, revise, preview, or discuss an email.
The intended recipient is anyone other than the fixed personal inbox.
The request needs HTML, remote attachment URLs, carbon copies, scheduling, or delivery tracking.
outcome: Resend accepts one immediate plain-text submission with the caller-provided subject, body, optional attachment bytes and optional reply metadata for the fixed recipient.
effects: Reads `RESEND_API_KEY` from the process environment and makes an authenticated network request to Resend.
Discloses the supplied subject, body, and any attachment filenames and bytes to Resend and the fixed recipient's Gmail provider.
Uses either a fresh generated idempotency key or a validated caller-supplied key in the Resend request.
Uses product-fixed sender and recipient addresses; callers cannot override either address.
Reads explicitly selected local regular files once before any network request and includes their filenames and exact bytes as attachments.
Optional reply_to, In-Reply-To and References values are validated and included in the same frozen provider request. They do not change the fixed sender or recipient.
authority: Email owns the fixed addresses, request construction, and command result.
A calling product owns its send authorization, occurrence state, exact message, and caller-supplied idempotency key; invoking Email does not create that authority.
Resend owns submission acceptance and its message record; Gmail owns final delivery and inbox receipt.
The caller owns authorization for the Reply-To mailbox and the meaning and exact ordered values of thread headers. Email accepts no arbitrary header map.
success: The command exits successfully and reports the Resend message identifier returned for the accepted submission.
When final receipt matters, the intended message is observed separately in the Gmail inbox.
failure_and_recovery: An input, authentication, transport, or Resend rejection exits unsuccessfully and reports a secret-safe error.
One invocation retries transport errors, rate limits, and server errors at most twice with the same frozen request and idempotency key.
Email has no delivery queue or retained message state; resolve the reported cause and retry only under the user's explicit request or the calling product's existing send authority.
After ambiguous transport failure, inspect Resend before retrying when avoiding a duplicate matters.
privacy: The exact subject, body, and any attachment filenames and bytes leave the machine for Resend and Gmail when the command sends.
A caller-supplied idempotency key also leaves the machine for Resend and must not contain secrets or message content.
Email does not retain the subject, body, attachments, or a delivery history in local product state.
The installed wrapper sources `~/.zshrc`, extracts only `RESEND_API_KEY`, and scrubs unrelated caller environment variables before starting the payload.
Only attachment basenames and captured contents are transmitted; local source paths are not included in the provider payload or error diagnostics.
Reply addresses and RFC thread IDs are disclosed to Resend and Gmail and remain part of the exact idempotent payload. Email retains no thread state.
Explicit local account setup can retain a private credential outside message history; email.account.operate owns that effect.

interfaces.label: Send body and attachment bytes from stdin
Send an answer in an email thread

does_not_authorize: Sending when the user requested only a draft, preview, revision, or explanation.
Treating the presence of `--idempotency-key` as scheduling authority, standing send authority, or retained occurrence state.
Changing the fixed sender, recipient, Resend account, or API key.
Treating Resend acceptance as proof of final Gmail delivery.

consumers.statement: The current user may send a supplied or approved message immediately, and an installed local product may send one exact frozen occurrence only under its own explicit standing authority.
A caller asking only to draft, revise, preview, discuss, schedule, track, or address another recipient cannot rely on this capability to send.

preconditions.statement: A real send requires explicit current-user authority or a calling product's documented standing authority, an approved exact subject and plain-text body, the product-fixed addresses, a valid RESEND_API_KEY, network access, and Resend availability. Any attachments must be authorized for disclosure and readable regular local files.
A supplied idempotency key already identifies the exact frozen product occurrence, contains no secret or message content, and satisfies the visible-ASCII length contract.

inputs.statement: The CLI requires a UTF-8 subject and plain-text body. A body value of '-' reads all standard input. The caller can supply an idempotency key. Repeat --attach PATH to capture each regular local file once. Transmitted names are UTF-8 basenames without control characters or path separators. Remote URLs are unsupported.
Recipients, senders, HTML, remote attachment URLs, carbon copies, schedules, drafts, previews, delivery callbacks, API keys in arguments, and hidden occurrence authority are not accepted inputs.

--payload-stdin with body - accepts one JSON object containing UTF-8 body and ordered attachments, each with filename and base64 content. It conflicts with --attach. Unknown fields, invalid base64 or unsafe filenames are rejected before network submission.

Optional --reply-to accepts one ASCII mailbox without a display name, at most 254 bytes with a 64-byte dot-atom local part and 63-byte DNS labels. --in-reply-to accepts one bracketed ASCII RFC Message-ID without whitespace, inner angle brackets, backslash or double quote, at most 998 bytes. Repeated --reference preserves order and allows at most 64 IDs and 8192 bytes including spaces. No arbitrary headers are accepted.

outputs.statement: When Resend accepts the message, Email exits zero and prints Accepted followed by the message ID. This confirms submission acceptance. Check Gmail separately for delivery. On failure, Email exits nonzero and reports a bounded error without the response body or credential.
Email returns no draft identity, queued occurrence, local send-history record, scheduled state, final Gmail receipt, delivery tracking result, or domain-success assertion for its caller.
The byte-payload path captures content in memory, submits through the same fixed-recipient transport, prints the same Accepted ID on acceptance and retains no local payload or history.

data_semantics.statement: A successful command means Resend accepted the exact frozen submission request; it does not mean Gmail delivered, classified, displayed, or retained the message.
The optional idempotency key identifies one caller-owned exact payload for Resend deduplication and does not create standing authority, scheduling, occurrence state, or Email-side retention.
Subject and body are caller-provided plain text; Email fixes both addresses and does not reinterpret the message as a requester-domain fact.

identity_and_units.statement: The Resend message ID identifies provider acceptance, a caller key identifies one exact frozen occurrence, and an ordinary invocation creates a fresh email/UUIDv7 request key.
A caller key contains 1 through 256 visible ASCII characters without whitespace, and one invocation makes at most three transport attempts using the identical key and request.
Email publishes no pricing, token, storage, or delivery-time measurement unit.
In-Reply-To and References contain RFC Message-IDs, not Resend provider IDs. Reply routing and ordered thread IDs belong to the exact payload identified by a supplied idempotency key.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Each invocation captures the subject, body, and attachment names and bytes, then immediately submits that unchanged request. It preserves standard input and reports acceptance or the final failure after bounded retries.
Email keeps no queue or local delivery history, so final receipt and any later provider state must be observed separately at Gmail or Resend.
No submission-latency, final-delivery-time, provider-availability, inbox-retention, or perpetual external idempotency-retention objective is promised.

access.statement: The supported surface is the current-user local Email CLI; the installed wrapper reads only RESEND_API_KEY from ~/.zshrc, preserves standard input, and starts the payload with a scrubbed minimal environment.
Help and version reads bypass credential loading, while a send makes an authenticated outbound Resend request and discloses the exact message to Resend and Gmail.
Chancery discovery, binary presence, API-key availability, or possession of an idempotency key grants no send authority or access to another address.

email::api::Client selects one absolute installed wrapper path and supplies content on stdin without reading RESEND_API_KEY. Direct free Rust functions use the caller environment credential. Both preserve fixed outbound addresses. api::recipient and api::sender expose those provider-owned values.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: One command freezes the request and selected key, submits immediately, and retries only transport errors, rate limits, and server errors at most twice using the identical bytes and key. Attachment order, filenames, and base64-encoded captured bytes are part of the frozen request; retries never reopen attachment files.
Within Resend's documented 24-hour key retention, the same key and payload deduplicate while changed payload under that key is rejected; Email stores no state to extend or reconstruct that window.
After ambiguous failure, the caller inspects Resend before any separately authorized retry when avoiding a duplicate matters; Email has no queued operation to resume.
Reply options remain frozen with the message and attachments across transport retries. Email does not retain or repair a thread; the receiving email client decides grouping.

operational_limits.statement: Each invocation supports one synchronous immediate plain-text message, one fixed sender, one fixed recipient, one optional bounded key, and no more than three attempts. Attachment bytes are held in memory for the invocation and remain subject to Resend message-size and file-type limits.
There is no draft, preview, HTML, remote attachment URL, copy, recipient option, scheduler, daemon, background retry queue, retained delivery database, or final-receipt observer.
No maximum message-size promise beyond provider acceptance, throughput objective, rate-limit allocation, or provider service-level objective is declared.

The typed installed-wrapper Client bounds each invocation to 120 seconds, receives at most 4096 receipt bytes, and performs no automatic process retry. Its timeout or process failure can leave send acceptance unknown. The transport does not follow redirects.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Capability contract version 4 adds optional local attachments while preserving plain-text invocation and caller-supplied idempotency behavior; Message and send remain source-compatible and send_with_attachments extends the Rust API.
No future API migration protocol, cross-release support interval, fixed external-provider retention policy, or deprecation window is promised.

Release 0.5.1 adds --payload-stdin to attachment contract 4. Existing subject/body and --attach invocations retain their behavior. Callers requiring byte input must check the selected executable advertises the new flag.

Contract 4 adds optional reply fields through ReplyOptions and send_with_options while preserving Message, send and send_with_attachments. The new receive list/get CLI forms are reserved; -- before send positionals preserves literal subjects that match a reserved form. Existing attachment and payload-stdin behavior remains supported.

reliances.statement: Immediate submission and acceptance reporting rely on Resend's authenticated network API, availability, retry semantics, idempotency behavior, and returned message record; no installed Chancery contract covers Resend.
Email does not rely on or observe Gmail to establish command success; final delivery, spam classification, and inbox receipt remain outside this promise and require separate observation.
